bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

news.label: Sin señales
news.summary: No hay anuncios ni reportes de trabajos de apertura en los Back Bowls. Vail abrió la temporada el 13 de noviembre con terreno limitado y el pronóstico solo trae nevadas ligeras esta semana.

sections.Key Messages:
- A quick-moving system is bringing snow to the mountains and
  some mountain valleys today with snowfall totals of 2 to 6
  inches with locally higher amounts.
- Travel conditions through passes could become very difficult
  at times. A Winter Weather Advisory is in effect for the San
  Juan Mountains and central Colorado mountains over 9,000 feet.
- Active weather remains possible late Thanksgiving week, but
  some details still remain uncertain. Stay tuned for updates to
  timing and impacts as they become available.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 1103 AM MST Mon Nov 23 2026
SNOW SHOWERS TODAY:
A fast-moving trough is making its way through the region today,
bringing with it another round of active weather. Looking at
cameras across the region, locations around and in the San Juans
have started to see impactful snow over the past several hours
with some areas sitting around 2-3 inches. Most roadways through
the San Juans are either wet or covered in snow at this point in
time, so expect for travel to be difficult at times should you
be driving through. By the time storms have moved out of
southwestern Colorado, snow accumulations are anticipated to sit
around 3-6 inches, though should banded snow develop, higher
accumulations cannot be ruled out. The possibility of stronger
snow bands is low to moderate at this time though primarily due
to lacking instability in areas northeast of the Four Corners.
Nonetheless, brief heavy snow rates remain in the realm of
possibility. We've already seen visibility drop to a quarter
mile in some areas due to snowfall, so even without heavy snow
rates, reduced visibility may develop at several locations. Due
to the already-present impacts across the San Juans combined
with increasing holiday travel, we have opted to issue a Winter
Weather Advisory for the San Juans above 9,000 feet until 6PM
today in spite of sub-advisory snow forecasts.
Throughout the course of the day, look for the bulk of active
weather to shift northeastwards into the central Colorado
mountains. Some CAM's remain bullish on moderate snowfall rates
making their way into the Sawatch Mountains and potentially over
Vail Pass, but we lean towards a middle-of-the-road outcome in
regards to snow accumulations, with snow totals at and below
pass level around I-70 resting below 4 inches. Due to
Thanksgiving travel ramping up though, even this amount of snow
could cause issues during travel, especially given how impactful
precipitation has been on major roadways over the past couple
weeks. Be weather aware and be prepared for tougher-than-normal
travel conditions today.
ANOTHER ROUND OF SNOW AFTER THANKSGIVING:
A deep, yet fast ridge develops during the mid-week, bringing an
end to precipitation region-wide. This precedes a late-week
system passing through the western CONUS, with the likeliest
arrival sometime on Friday. Unfortunately, deterministic models
are still struggling to come to an agreement on the nature of
this storm. What is apparent is the development of high pressure
off the SoCal coast and split flow across the Intermountain
West. Where this split flow and resulting quieter weather occurs
is highly uncertain at this point. Should it dip far enough
south for strong northwesterly flow to establish itself over the
CWA, we could see favorable orographics support snowfall over
the Park Range. This looks to be the most likely scenario at
this time, but with the upper-level pattern being so complex,
there is too little confidence to bank on this outcome coming to
fruition. That being said, the probability of snowfall during
the late-week period is increasing, and so if you are planning
to travel during this time, be prepared for the possibility of
difficult travel conditions, especially over the northern
Colorado mountains and maybe even across other portions of the
CWA as well. Stay tuned over the coming days for additional
updates.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 1029 AM MST Mon Nov 23 2026
Rain and snow showers are ongoing for terminals south of I-70.
These precipitation chances will creep northward this afternoon,
creating reduced visibilities and lowered cigs. With that being
said, terminals south of I-70 have the best chance of
circulating between MVFR/IFR flight categories with cigs
falling below ILS breakpoints. LIFR conditions remain a
possibility with brief bursts of heavier snow. Precipitation
chances taper off by ~01Z, giving way to decreased cloud cover
as we move into Tuesday. Light, terrain-driven winds will
prevail for the next 24 hours.
